elements.element: No more than one audit in any twelve-month period
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor may not request more than one audit in any twelve-month period.

elements.element: Audit request must be in writing
elements.evidence: The audit is triggered by Licensee's receipt of a written request from Licensor.

elements.element: At least 30 days' advance notice of an audit
elements.evidence: The clause requires Licensee to permit the audit within 30 days after receiving the request, which allows an immediate audit and does not provide 30 days' advance notice.

elements.element: Audit must be conducted during Customer's business hours
elements.evidence: Each audit must be conducted during Licensee's normal business hours.

elements.element: Audit must be conducted by an independent auditor
elements.evidence: The clause specifies an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional selected by mutual agreement.

elements.element: The independent auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations
elements.evidence: The audit is generally made subject to the Agreement's confidentiality obligations, but the clause does not expressly require the non-party auditor to be bound by confidentiality.

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit cost by default
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor bears the audit cost unless the specified discrepancy threshold is met.

elements.element: Customer may bear the audit cost only if an underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: Cost shifts upon any discrepancy exceeding 5%, not specifically an underpayment exceeding 5%.

elements.element: The auditor may not directly access Customer's systems
elements.evidence: The clause permits auditing and analyzing accounting records but contains no prohibition on direct access to Licensee's systems.
The rolling cap of no more than one audit in any twelve-month period is at least as protective as a once-per-year cap.

elements.element: At least 15 days' advance notice of an audit
elements.evidence: Although a written request is required, the audit may occur at any time within 30 days after receipt; no minimum 15-day advance period is provided.

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit cost by default
elements.evidence: Licensor bears the audit cost unless the stated cost-shifting condition applies.

elements.element: Customer may bear the audit cost only if an underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: The clause shifts cost for any discrepancy exceeding 5%, which is broader and has a lower threshold than an underpayment exceeding 10%.

result.reason: Neither position is fully achieved. The redline adds a rolling annual cap and business-hours restriction, but “within 30 days” is a deadline for permitting the audit rather than advance notice. It also fails to bind the auditor expressly to confidentiality, prohibit direct systems access, or use the required underpayment-based cost trigger. The fallback 10% threshold is likewise absent. The language generally preserves the original audit arrangement without introducing a direct contradiction, but its notice and confidentiality drafting is imprecise.
